32b37e4.summary: Sends the PUNReceiveWrongRoom RPC to all players in the room (including ourselves), seemingly to tell clients they are in the wrong room. Called from BattleCommsManager; the rest is inlined Photon RPC sending code plus interest-group and event-cache helpers the decompiler glued on.
comments: Set up an empty argument list and the RPC name PUNReceiveWrongRoom; this RPC carries no parameters.
Photon safety checks: do nothing if the network cannot be used right now.
Not inside a room: log 'RPCs can only be sent in rooms' and give up.
No networking peer yet (e.g. scene loading): log an error and give up.
Skip the send if this view's interest group is blocked for sending.
View ID is not valid (< 1): log 'Illegal view ID' error, the RPC is not sent.
Only builds the verbose 'Sending RPC' log string when log level is Full; both paths continue at the event build.
Build the Photon RPC event: view ID, optional prefix, server timestamp, then the method name or its short id.
If the RPC name has a registered shortcut, send the compact id instead of the full name.
Raise Photon event 200 (RPC) reliably on the view's interest group; this reaches every player in the room.
PhotonTargets.All also runs the RPC locally, so execute it for our own actor too.
Shared failure target: a null reference somewhere in the send path ends here.
Verbose-log path: builds 'Sending RPC <name> to target ...' and logs it, then rejoins the send code.
Decompiler run-on: the code below is a different inlined method, NetworkingPeer.SetInterestGroups, not part of this send.
Groups to remove: an empty array clears all; otherwise remove each valid group (0 is rejected) from the set.
Groups to add: an empty array means subscribe to every group 0-255; otherwise add each valid group.
Outside offline mode, forward the new group lists to the server.
Decompiler run-on: below is another inlined method, an event-cache hash lookup (remove/add of a cache entry).
Remove branch: find the entry by hash in the bucket chain and unlink it onto the free list.
Add branch: look for an existing entry first; if absent, take a free slot (growing the table if full) and insert.

32b38ac.summary: Sends a PlayerAction to everyone (including ourselves) by packing its seven fields into an object array and calling the PUNReceivePlayerAction RPC. Called whenever the local player performs a game action that must be replayed on the opponent's client.
comments: Array of 7 RPC arguments, in the order the receiver expects.
Argument 0 is typ (the action type); then act, tget, tgtd (target data, boxed), pos, num, at follow in order.
Each store is bounds-checked by the compiler; running out of space ends at the InvalidOperationException below.
Send as PUNReceivePlayerAction to PhotonTargets.All, so the action also executes locally via Photon.
Array index/cast check failure path.
Null reference path (action, array or photonView was null).

32b3b78.summary: Logs the last action counter received and sends it via the PUNReceiveResendLostActions RPC to all players, asking the sender to resend actions we missed. Called when the client notices a gap in the action sequence. The decompiler then runs on into the body of SendForfeit.
comments: Log a warning with the last action counter we received (the anti-cheat wrapped value is read out).
One RPC argument: our last received action counter, boxed.
Box check from the decompiler; the normal path stores the counter and sends the RPC.
Ask for lost actions: PUNReceiveResendLostActions to all, carrying our last received counter.
Decompiler run-on: from here the code is the start of SendForfeit (PUNReceiveEnemyForfeit), not part of this method.
